Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)

Architecting systems where humans can approve, edit, or reject the agent's actions before they happen.

Breakpoints

You can configure LangGraph to interrupt execution before or after specific nodes. This is essential for sensitive actions (e.g., sending an email, deploying code). 

# Interrupt before the 'action' node runs
graph = workflow.compile(
    checkpointer=memory,
    interrupt_before=["action_node"]
)

Review Workflow

When the graph pauses, the state is saved. A human can inspect the state, and then simply call stream() or invoke() with Command(resume=...) to continue.

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Agent participant ActionNode User->>Agent: "Send email to Bob" Agent->>Agent: Draft Email Agent-->>ActionNode: Ready to Send Note right of ActionNode: INTERRUPT! User->>Agent: Review Draft User->>Agent: "Approve (Resume)" Agent->>ActionNode: Execute Send ActionNode->>User: "Email Sent"

State Editing

Humans can do more than just approve. They can modify the state. For example, if the agent drafted a bad email, the human can update the messages list in the checkpoint to replace the draft with a better one, then resume execution.
